fundamental.method_reasoning: Multi-stage FCF DCF is the right frame for an asset-light subscription business with 34.7% FCF margin, 1.4%-of-revenue capex and 193% FCF/NI conversion. The caveats are inputs, not method: SBC is untagged anywhere in the extract so reported FCF is almost certainly overstated relative to owner earnin

band_dissents.reasoning: The engine used 15.8% because that is the single-year FCF growth print, but FCF growth of that magnitude came from margin expansion (operating margin +105bps, gross margin +48bps) and working-capital/capex leverage, not from volume. Revenue grew 9.6% and the Q1 annualized run-rate of $44.53B against $41.52B FY implies the same high-single-digit trajectory. Margin-driven FCF growth cannot compound for five years at 15.8% off a 34.7% FCF margin base without implying a >50% FCF margin by Y5; the durable rate is the revenue rate, modestly aided by residual mix, i.e. 7-10%.

A five-year explicit high-growth stage is reasonable for a franchise with 77.7% gross margin and stable 14.4%-of-revenue R&D reinvestment, but the case for the full five years weakens if growth is set at the revenue rate rather than the margin-inflated FCF rate. Three to five years is the acceptable band; the engine's 5 sits at the permissive end rather than being wrong.

wacc.reasoning: 9.0% was calibrated for the pre-recapitalization, roughly net-cash-neutral company. Debt/equity moved from 0.244 to 1.147 in one quarter and total debt from $14.44B to $39.28B, with tangible book deeply negative and post-deal interest expense literally unavailable (the current-quarter interest tag is flagged STALE). Levered equity beta on 819M shares is materially higher than before; the discount rate for this duration asset should sit near or above the 9.5-11% range until the actual coupon on ~$29B of new borrowing is disclosed.

g_terminal.reasoning: Terminal value is $759.80B of a $507.45B EV base — PV of terminal is roughly 63% of EV and any TV-heavy model must be conservative here. The CRM category is described as growing ~9.5% toward ~$69B, i.e. a market Salesforce already substantially occupies at $41.52B of revenue; a perpetual 3.0% real-plus-inflation claim assumes indefinite share retention against seat-model AI disruption the filings neither confirm nor deny. 2.0-2.5% is the defensible band for a mature enterprise application franchise.

base_fcf_method.reasoning: The $14.40B TTM base is the peak of a three-year ramp ($9.50B → $12.43B → $14.40B) and, critically, SBC is not tagged in any period, so this FCF is unadjusted for what is typically 8-10% of revenue in dilution for a software filer. It also embeds a fiscal-year-end AR peak of $14.34B (+20.0% YoY) whose collection flatters cash conversion. A 3-year average base is the honest mid-cycle anchor and partially offsets the SBC omission the engine cannot correct.

fade_years.reasoning: A five-year linear fade from high growth to terminal is appropriate for subscription revenue with high switching costs; if anything a longer fade is arguable given the installed base, but 5 years is defensible and is not where the model's sensitivity lives.
